guardrails.title: Detached validation at the checkpoint tag
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: The documented tag-checkout validation procedure to fail again.

guardrails.title: File inventory recomputed from the repository
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: An undeclared or silently altered file to ship inside a valid checkpoint.

guardrails.title: Every finalization attempt is recorded, including a refusal
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A refused operation to disappear from the ledger.

guardrails.title: Readiness and blockage are mutually exclusive
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A checkpoint to claim readiness and blockage at once.

guardrails.title: The Gate specification lives in the repository
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A Gate to be accepted against a specification that is not in the repository.

guardrails.title: A control over its own run's evidence is scoped to handoff
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A control over a checkpoint's own evidence to be invalidated by the evidence its own run produces, and to be green under one runner of the mandatory gates while red under another.

guardrails.title: A PASS resolves its evidence
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A PASS with no execution behind it.

guardrails.title: An external verdict is derived from an attestation
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: An implementing run to certify itself as externally validated.

guardrails.title: The expected requirement set is derived independently
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A delivery to shrink its own denominator and claim total coverage.

guardrails.title: The mandatory gate set is closed by policy
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A red or unexecuted gate to be handed to the auditor as green.

guardrails.title: A recorded command binds its inputs by content
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A ledger that cannot be replayed at the commit it names.

guardrails.title: Sealed history is anchored outside the content it describes
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A coordinated tag and content move to pass as untouched history.

guardrails.title: Sealing is monotonic and post-commit
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: Final evidence to describe a state that was never sealed.

guardrails.title: One promotion invariant covers every positive terminal status
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A new terminal status to start life with no rules.

guardrails.title: A gate run is measured against the canonical mandatory set
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: An invocation to decide how much of the mandatory set actually runs.

guardrails.title: The denominator comes from a source the delivery does not own
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: Coverage to be computed over whatever set the delivery chose to submit.

guardrails.title: A structured reference is resolved, not merely typed
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A guardrail claim to name a control that does not exist.

guardrails.title: A derived artifact carries a fingerprint of its inputs
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A stale selection to survive the change that invalidated it.

guardrails.title: Evidence from a dirty tree carries immutable input identity
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A record to name a commit that never held what the command read.

guardrails.title: The sealed checkpoint chain is re-derived from Git
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: Sealed history to be rewritten with every dependent value refreshed.

guardrails.title: An evidential count is derived and verified where it is stated
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: Two artifacts to state different numbers for the same fact.

guardrails.title: Lesson provenance resolves against the checkpoint it cites
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A lesson to cite a source that does not record the finding it claims.

guardrails.title: The positive promotion path is executed, not only the refusals
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A status-gating control whose positive path is unreachable to look complete because every forgery is refused.

guardrails.title: The pending-anchor exclusion is derived from repository state
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A guardrail to depend on the checkpoint name that happened to be newest when it was written.

guardrails.title: An adversarial battery records a null-mutation control
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A battery whose refusals come from a broken fixture to be read as defences.

guardrails.title: No comment or docstring states a derived count
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A cardinality maintained by hand in a source file to contradict the derivation without any control noticing.

guardrails.title: A GUARDED lesson may not describe itself as unguarded
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A lesson's prose to state the opposite of the status the tooling reads.

guardrails.title: The memory policy declares only settings the implementation reads
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A documented configuration key that changes nothing to survive as if it were behaviour.

guardrails.title: The protocol's own next steps are executed before handoff
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A required protocol transition to turn a mandatory gate red in the next delivery instead of this one.

guardrails.title: An empty applicable set is told from a missing required set
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A delivery with nothing of a kind to audit to be refused for having nothing to audit, or a delivery with work still open to declare that work away.

guardrails.title: A simulation executes the control it claims passed
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A rehearsal to report a control as passing while the control itself refuses every real delivery.

guardrails.title: The transition into the next Gate is executed before handoff
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: The first delivery of the next Gate to discover, after the Gate starts, that it cannot be handed over at all.

guardrails.title: The application declares only configuration its own source reads
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A configuration key that promises behaviour nothing implements to ship as if it were a feature, in the application as well as in the policy documents.

guardrails.title: Scope is judged against a registry of Gate reservations, not a literal
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A later Gate's capability to be implemented early with nothing to notice, and the scope control to keep refusing the Gate that legitimately fills a directory.

guardrails.title: An error produced outside the middleware chain still carries its correlation
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A failure response to tell a caller to quote an identifier that the response does not contain, making the safe error message unactionable.

guardrails.title: Request metrics are labelled with the route the router actually matched
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: Every request to be labelled with one bucket while the metrics endpoint keeps answering and the dashboard keeps rendering.

guardrails.title: Every subprocess capture, and every tool that re-emits one, states its codec
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A tool to abort with a Unicode error while reading or printing output it was only meant to pass along, discarding work that had already succeeded.

guardrails.title: A gate that measures inside an image builds that image first
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A mandatory gate to report PASS about source that is not in the repository, so a red test can be committed and sealed behind a green gate.

guardrails.title: A shared control derives every identifier it reasons about
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A control to name today's Gate, checkpoint or migration revision, so it refuses the next one and gets edited out of the way rather than corrected.

guardrails.title: One definition of what a credential-carrying name is, and one home for it
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: Modules to answer 'does this name carry a credential' differently from one another, which hid whether a real credential had reached the committed example file and redacted an operational limit out of the configuration dump.

guardrails.title: The operational catalog holds only providers the policy declares
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: Test fixtures to accumulate in the operator-visible catalog, where a route could resolve to a model that does not exist.

guardrails.title: Every anchored checkpoint validates from its own tag in a clone of the published history
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A sealed checkpoint to stop validating from its own tag, or to validate only on the machine whose object store still holds a commit no published reference reaches, without anything noticing until a clone of the remote is verified (M1-F-003).

guardrails.title: No source file carries a stray control character, and every scan asserts it found something
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A control whose pattern was mangled in editing to match nothing, compile, run and report the delivery as clean.

guardrails.title: A migration is applied and reversed against a disposable database, so a constraint name mismatch is a failing test
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A migration that applies and cannot be reversed, discovered during the incident that needed the reversal.

guardrails.title: A scenario waits on the server's answer rather than on another process's log line
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A scenario to start work against a queue nobody polls, time out, and report a defect that does not exist.

guardrails.title: Every boundary scan reads the syntax tree and carries a control that fires on a mutated module
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A boundary scan to be weakened until it passes, or to be satisfied by a docstring, with nothing showing that it can still fail.

guardrails.title: No counted pytest suite expands at run time
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A counted suite to declare cases the denominator cannot see, so the whole ledger errors on a message that names the counter rather than the file.

guardrails.title: A run that outlives its deadline reaches a terminal state and the store records why
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A run to hit its deadline, die silently, and leave a row RUNNING for ever — which reads from outside exactly like a deadline that was never enforced.

guardrails.title: An envelope refusal names the defect it found, and the contract names the type of content
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A wrong-typed content to be refused as missing again, so the one repair quotes a false reason and a model that answered with an array fails the run with the same array.

guardrails.title: No terminal run state is visible before the terminal event that explains it
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A reader that waits for a terminal state to find a log that never says the run ended, and an SSE stream opened on a finished run to close without its terminal event.

guardrails.title: Every check of what Prometheus observes waits for a scrape, within a bound, and asks only Prometheus
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A smoke to pass or fail by how long the stack had been running - the gateway smoke on a rebuilt stack, the Foundation smoke on a fresh installation - and a green check to mean only that the timing was lucky.

guardrails.title: A checkpoint is sealed only when its state names its own tag, and validates from it
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A checkpoint to be sealed in a state from which it can never be validated, discovered only when a successor anchors it and the historical check turns red for good.

guardrails.title: What a service hands another is bounded as the receiver measures it
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A tool result inside the sandbox's own bound to fail the run that asked for it, because the runtime measures it larger.

guardrails.title: The execute activity's result is named once and used on both sides of the queue
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: The workflow and the sandbox to drift into incompatible shapes that every double-driven suite still passes, discovered only when a real run's workflow task fails.

guardrails.title: The sweep freezes before it kills, and a detached fork bomb leaves a usable sandbox
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A command that detaches a fork bomb to leave its sandbox unable to start another process for the rest of the run.

guardrails.title: The envelope contract every model receives is rendered from the schema the parser enforces
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A model to be asked, again, for a shape it is never shown — or for one written by hand beside the schema that drifts from what the parser accepts.

guardrails.title: A tool result is accepted only from the executor that owns the request
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A result posted to the API to displace the sandbox's own, so an agent acts on a tool outcome that never happened.

guardrails.title: Critical and High dependency advisories remain release-blocking
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A pinned graph with a current Critical or High advisory, or an unavailable advisory source, to be handed off as green.

guardrails.title: Host-published services are exercised through their real loopback ports
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A stack whose containers are healthy but whose host-published ports close every connection to be reported as operational.

guardrails.title: Lesson preflight exclusions declare their scope
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A technology or module selector to silently exclude an active lesson without declaring the scope boundary reviewers must evaluate.

guardrails.title: Parent facts are flushed before child facts without an ORM dependency edge
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A store to add parent and child facts by raw UUID in one unit of work and discover only in production PostgreSQL that the child insert can precede its parent.

guardrails.title: Running cancellation records cleanup acknowledgement before completion
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A running task to claim cancellation completed before its executor has entered and acknowledged the cleanup phase.

guardrails.title: Evidence provenance deduplicates equal content digests
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: Distinct source roles carrying identical bytes to produce an invalid duplicate sourceDigests tuple and abort evidence persistence.

guardrails.title: Cross-service quality execution identities are stable UUIDs
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A semantically valid quality check identity to be rejected by the sandbox's UUID persistence boundary, or to change across a retry.

guardrails.title: Every sandbox session has exactly one real run owner
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: An evaluator session to invent a task-run owner, have two owners, have none, or bypass the one-active-session invariant.

guardrails.title: Evaluator requests never bind the agent-only active request foreign key
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A quality request to be rejected because its stable execution identity has no unrelated agent tool_requests row.

guardrails.title: Plan reuse compares immutable material rather than observation metadata
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: The same snapshot and policy to conflict with their own frozen plan merely because another request observed them later or under another owner.

guardrails.title: Acknowledged activity cancellation remains cancellation through Temporal wrapping
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A cleanup-acknowledged cancellation to be persisted as an evaluator error merely because Temporal delivered it through ActivityError.

guardrails.title: Manifest limits apply only to files the detector interprets as manifests
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: An unrelated large source, policy or generated record to make an otherwise supported repository impossible to evaluate before any quality check runs.

guardrails.title: Polyglot plans bind every check to its detected root and policy-owned toolchain
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A supported polyglot monorepo to be refused as an unknown combination, or to execute a check from the wrong directory or in the wrong toolchain image.

guardrails.title: Project roots and unit applicability come from the frozen source inventory
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: Nested fixtures to execute as products, empty suites to fail as if tests failed, or a real suite to be suppressed as non-applicable.

guardrails.title: Every isolated quality check works on the oldest pinned helper runtime
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A shared helper to crash in one pinned image or a check to rely on dependencies that existed only in a sandbox already released.

guardrails.title: Quality images share the policy-owned secret taxonomy and allowance set
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: Two mandatory secret gates to contradict each other on the same bytes or a project-authored allowance to hide an actual credential.

guardrails.title: Mandatory lint intersects every detected non-fixture Python project root
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A green lint verdict to describe only a manually selected subset while a detected project root accumulates unchecked findings.

guardrails.title: Nested Python tests receive package metadata and repository policy inside the sandbox
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A source-import-only environment to fail tests that require installed metadata or repository-root configuration despite having all immutable snapshot bytes.

guardrails.title: Offline Python metadata installation has a pinned build backend
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A no-network quality run to fail before tests because the project build backend exists only on the public package index or by accident in a base image.

guardrails.title: Projected nested policy does not replace the trusted repository root
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A nested compatibility projection to be mistaken for repository ownership and silently shrink a source-boundary scan to zero files.

guardrails.title: Large functional workflows have separate finite wait bounds
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A legitimate large quality or sandbox workflow to outlive a fixture-sized harness wait and be reported as an infrastructure failure before its durable verdict.

guardrails.title: Recorded subjects resolve and provenance inputs are canonical
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A command to execute while its evidence names a nonexistent commit, or repeated caller inputs to produce non-canonical provenance.

guardrails.title: Unit collection covers the scope that made the check applicable
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A recognized root-level test to make a unit check mandatory while the runner collects only a narrower directory and reports a vacuous PASS.

guardrails.title: Verification stages clear reusable reports before execution
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A failed current stage to leave an older PASS artifact at the path reviewers treat as the current report.

guardrails.title: Canonical requirement evidence resolves to discovered tests
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A canonical requirement to cite an intended test label that no declared suite executes.

guardrails.title: Engineering memory cites no ephemeral var report
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A lesson to become invalid whenever a verifier clears or replaces the current generated report under var.

guardrails.title: Captured UTF-8 is re-emitted through an explicitly configured stream
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A successful child command to make its Windows entry point fail while printing decoded non-ASCII output.

guardrails.title: Historical Gate documentation tests derive current entry-point state
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A predecessor regression test to require its historical next state from the repository's current entry point.

guardrails.title: Source controls compare syntax semantics, not formatter layout
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A formatter-only line break or quote change to make a semantic source control reject correct code.

guardrails.title: Empty subprocess streams retain the exit diagnostic
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A subprocess-backed assertion to erase the only observable failure fact when stdout and stderr are both empty.

guardrails.title: Rehearsal workers register the shared workflow's quality boundary
guardrails.removingItWouldAllow: A purpose-built worker to resume the shared workflow and then fail on an unregistered post-run activity, leaving its durable row nonterminal.
